column1: # Every question shape, in every shipped language.
# The localized files before this one were thin and uneven: Swedish had breadth, the other ten
# languages had a handful of rows each, and whole shapes — aggregates, isotopes, nuclides, unit
# requests, deferrals — went untested outside English. A defect in those languages could only be
# This file is deliberately the *same* twenty-two shapes in each language, so a gap shows up as a
# row of failures across one language rather than as scattered noise, and so the shapes can be
# compared against their English equivalents directly.
# Languages the author cannot verify to a native standard — af, fil, hi, ur, zh — are marked in
# docs/TRANSLATION_REVIEW.md. Their rows are still worth having: a query that resolves nothing at
# all is a defect regardless of how idiomatic the phrasing is.
